newsitem.title: USA: Texans held for allegedly smuggling deaf Mexicans.
newsitem.headline: Texans held for allegedly smuggling deaf Mexicans.

text.p: A Dallas couple was arrested on charges of smuggling Mexicans who cannot hear or speak into the United States, where they were made to peddle trinkets on the street for slave wages, officials said on Friday.
U.S. Attorney Paul Coggins said Victor and Maria Estela Cervantes -- themselves deaf -- were arrested on Thursday while driving a van carrying five illegal aliens from Mexico who were deaf and mute.
The couple was charged with knowingly transporting and harboring illegal aliens.

The Cervanteses had come under investigation after one deaf woman gave police details on smuggling rings that exploit the Mexicans by promising them a better life in the United States, only to sell them into virtual servitude.
The trade was exposed last month, when about 60 deaf-mute immigrants were found held in servitude in New York.
Since then, similar groups have been found across the United States, and several people have been arrested.
